subject: Culture
title: Blood Money Traditions
description: Learn Blood Money Traditions in one minute.

hook.text: In Saudi Arabia a murder charge can be dropped if the victim's family accepts financial compensation.

buildup.text: Blood money—called 'diya' in Islamic law—predates Islam. Anglo-Saxons had 'wergild' for the same purpose.

discovery.text: The logic: punishment should restore the victim's family, not satisfy the state's desire for vengeance.

twist.text: Critics call it a loophole for the rich. Defenders say it reduces cycles of revenge killing.

climax.text: Restorative justice programs in Norway follow the same principle—healing over punishment.

punchline.text: Every culture prices a life differently.

quiz.question: What is the Islamic legal term for blood money?
